title: SCNet P0 R06 paired single-factor diagnostics at 800 and 2000 m/s, 0.75 mm
purpose: Two paired single-factor diagnostics represented by four independent solver jobs; diagnostic attribution only, not a production P0 response set.

provenance.identity_rule: Every R06 job uses the original R05 case mesh, coordinates, connectivity, node IDs, element IDs, PIDs, material, EOS, contact, section, timestep, and boundary conditions except for its one preregistered factor.

symmetry.validity: normal incidence, face-on cube, centered impact only

intfor.interpretation_boundary: INTFOR pressure, force, gap, and penetration fields are direct solver diagnostics when present; NPEN support and sign conventions must be confirmed on the returned R15.0.2 files.

paired_experiments.question: Was the R05 800 m/s response censored by the 0.04 ms observation horizon?

preregistered_evaluation.prefix_check: Through 0.04 ms, the paired trajectories and event ledger must agree within the frozen numerical comparison tolerances; otherwise do not attribute suffix differences solely to the observation horizon.
preregistered_evaluation.treatment_question: Measure new first-crossing mass, deletion, ambiguity, and qM/qP/qE/qV evolution from 0.04 to 0.08 ms.
preregistered_evaluation.support_condition: The extended suffix reaches the existing tail-stability gates without worsening run-integrity, while the paired prefix is consistent.
preregistered_evaluation.refute_condition: The extended suffix remains unstable, adds material crossing/deletion, or the paired prefix is inconsistent.
preregistered_evaluation.claim_boundary: A stable longer window cannot recover a primary QoI while deleted-upstream mass remains above 5%. It cannot establish V50 or physical validity.

paired_experiments.question: How much of the 2000 m/s fragment loss is caused by eroding-contact automatic negative-volume deletion?

preregistered_evaluation.primary_contrast: Fragment negative-volume events, deleted-upstream reference mass, first-event time/location, and normal termination in treatment minus paired control.
preregistered_evaluation.mechanism_alignment: For each deleted solid, align the MES category, last alive MAT_015 damage D, D3PART state interval, and available INTFOR contact diagnostics. Do not impose an arbitrary D>=0.95 proxy for D=1.
preregistered_evaluation.support_condition: Fragment negative-volume events materially decrease while paired physics and run-integrity remain valid; residual other failures remain reported rather than relabeled.
preregistered_evaluation.refute_condition: Fragment negative-volume events do not decrease, the treatment terminates abnormally, or residual unresolved failures dominate without improved mass accounting.
preregistered_evaluation.historical_lower_bound: Even eliminating all 76 historical fragment negative-volume events leaves an element-count proxy of (448-76)/686 = 54.227% upstream deletion; therefore this is attribution, not an expected 5% gate repair.
preregistered_evaluation.claim_boundary: PSFAIL does not calibrate material failure, prove perforation, or create an admissible training label.

submission_sequence.wave_1_gate: Both controls must pass target-solver parsing, normal termination, required-output readability, and reproduce the relevant R05 failure pattern directionally before interventions are interpreted.
submission_sequence.resource_identity: Use exactly one node, 32 ranks, LS-DYNA R15 MPP double precision, and identical memory settings for all four jobs.

deferred_not_generated.reason: Changing the contact family weakens treatment of newly exposed eroding surfaces and can invalidate late response; reserve for a pre-deletion contact-mechanism study if the window diagnostic is inconclusive.

deferred_not_generated.candidate: 2000 m/s fragment MAT_015 EROD=0 versus EROD=1 ablation
deferred_not_generated.reason: EROD=1 retains failed mass with zeroed deviatoric stress, so its capture response cannot be used as a production QoI; reserve for a later material-failure attribution study.

claim_boundary: Four jobs implement two paired single-factor diagnostics; they are not four independent calibration points.
Static validation establishes serialization and identity only, not LS-DYNA parser/runtime acceptance.
A solver-completed diagnostic is not automatically an admissible P0 response.
The generic 4340 material and generic-steel EOS remain unvalidated for the real target system.
Unavailable response is never replaced with zero and targeted diagnostic data stay outside the reference response distribution.
